Exam

Each week we will provide a short task to test your knowledge, these should be used to guide your study for the final exam.

The task is to manipulate some raster data and produce some descriptive statistics. Climatic models fed into the latest Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the models are divided into Shared Socioeconomic Pathways known as SSPs, ranging from SSP1 (lots of mitigation and adaption) to SSP5 (fossil fuel development). The Carbon Brief explainer has more information on the scenarios.

For any country in the World produce descriptive statistics that show the difference in maximum temperature for key cities between SSP1 and SSP5 for the years 2081-2100, using any model and resolution.

WorldClim future projections
Country outlines
World city points


# Plan
Task : For any country in the World produce descriptive statistics that show the difference in maximum temperature for key cities between SSP1 and SSP5 for the years 2081-2100, using any model and resolution.

1. Collecting data:
  * GCM (MPI-ESM1-2-HR & MRI-ESM2-0) : tx data
  * wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_MPI-ESM1-2-HR_ssp126_2081-2100.tif ~ wc2.1_2.5m_tmax_MPI-ESM1-2-HR_ssp585_2081-2100.tif
  Geom data:
  * Country outlines (United Kingdom geopackage) : gadm41_GBR.gpkg
  * World cities: World_Cities.csv
 
2. Vector data loading
3. Raster (GCM) data loading
  Raster location with cities point
** Sync coordiate reference systems (CRS)**
4. Descriptive statistics
  4.1 Data preparation
  4.2 Histogram
  4.3 Using more data
  4.4 Histogram with ggplot

# 2. Vector data loading
```{r}
library(sf) 
library(here)
st_layers("week3_data/gadm41_GBR.gpkg")

library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
ukOutline <- st_read("week3_data/gadm41_GBR.gpkg", 
                      layer='ADM_ADM_0') # select outline layer

print(ukOutline) # to get Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
st_crs(ukOutline)$proj4string # to get proj4 string
```

```{r}
print(ukOutlinePROJECTED)
```

# 3.1 list Data loading
```{r}
# look in our folder, find the files that end with .tif and
library(fs)
dir_info("week3_data/")


library(tidyverse)

  filter(str_detect(path, ".tif")) %>%

ssp5 <- rast(listfiles[str_detect(listfiles, "ssp585")])
```

# 3.2 Raster location
```{r}
library(sf)
# Load cities data
ukCities <- read_csv('week3_data/World_Cities.csv') %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  filter(fips_cntry == 'UK')

# convert to sf and set correct CRS
ukcitiesSf <- ukCities %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3857) %>%
  st_transform(4326) # same as raster data



# Extract the data from the Rasterstack for all points 
ukCitySSP1 <- terra::extract(ssp1, vect(ukcitiesSf))
ukCitySSP5 <- terra::extract(ssp5, vect(ukcitiesSf))

# Add city name
ukCitySSP1 <- ukCitySSP1 %>% 
  as_tibble()%>% 
  add_column(Site = ukCities$city_name, .before = "Jan")

ukCitySSP5 <- ukCitySSP5 %>% 
  as_tibble()%>% 
  add_column(Site = ukCities$city_name, .before = "Jan")

```

# 4.3 Using more data (mapping)
```{r}
ukOutSIMPLE <- ukOutline %>%
  st_simplify(., dTolerance = 1000) %>%
  st_geometry()%>%
  plot()

# Check if same CRS
print(ukOutline)
#this works nicely for rasters
crs(ssp1)

ukTempSSP1 <- ukOutline %>%
  # now crop our temp data to the extent
  terra::crop(ssp1,.)

# plot the output
```

# 4.4 Histogram with ggplot

```{r}
ggplot() +
  # function from tidyterra
  geom_spatraster(
    # the raster 
    data = ukTempSSP1,
    # the layer within the raster
    aes(fill = Mar)
  )

# chage to data frame
ukTempSSP1df <- ukTempSSP1 %>%
  as.data.frame()


library(ggplot2)
# set up the basic histogram
gghist <- ggplot(ukTempSSP1df, 
                 aes(x=Mar)) + 
  geom_histogram(color="black", 
                 fill="white")+
  labs(title="Ggplot2 histogram of UK March temperatures", 
       x="Temperature", 
       y="Frequency")
# add a vertical line to the hisogram showing mean tempearture
gghist + geom_vline(aes(xintercept=mean(Mar, 
                                        na.rm=TRUE)),
            color="blue", 
            linetype="dashed", 
            size=1)+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

```{r}
# Make long data
squishdata<- ukTempSSP1df %>%
  pivot_longer(
  cols = 1:12,
  names_to = "Month",
  values_to = "Temp"
)

# Then subset the data, selecting two months using filter() from dplyr
twomonths <- squishdata %>%
  # | = OR
  filter(., Month=="Jan" | Month=="Jun")

meantwomonths <- twomonths %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(mean=mean(Temp, na.rm=TRUE))

meantwomonths


ggplot(twomonths, aes(x=Temp, color=Month, fill=Month)) +
  geom_histogram(position="identity", alpha=0.5)+
  geom_vline(data=meantwomonths, 
             aes(xintercept=mean, 
                 color=Month),
             linetype="dashed")+
  labs(title="Ggplot2 histogram of UK Jan and Jun
       temperatures",
       x="Temperature",
       y="Frequency")+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

data_complete_cases <- squishdata %>%
  drop_na()%>% 
  mutate(Month = factor(Month, levels = c("Jan","Feb","Mar",
                                          "Apr","May","Jun",
                                          "Jul","Aug","Sep",
                                          "Oct","Nov","Dec")))

# Plot faceted histogram
ggplot(data_complete_cases, aes(x=Temp, na.rm=TRUE))+
  geom_histogram(color="black", binwidth = 5)+
  labs(title="Ggplot2 faceted histogram of UK temperatures from SSP1", 
       x="Temperature",
       y="Frequency")+
  facet_grid(Month ~ .)+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))


```
# Interactive table
```{r}
library(plotly)
# split the data for plotly based on month

jan <- squishdata %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(., Month=="Jan")

jun <- squishdata %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(., Month=="Jun")

# give axis titles
x <- list (title = "Temperature")
y <- list (title = "Frequency")

# set the bin width
xbinsno<-list(start=0, end=40, size = 2.5)

# plot the histogram calling all the variables we just set
ihist<-plot_ly(alpha = 0.6) %>%
        add_histogram(x = jan$Temp,
        xbins=xbinsno, name="January") %>%
        add_histogram(x = jun$Temp,
        xbins=xbinsno, name="June") %>% 
        layout(barmode = "overlay", xaxis=x, yaxis=y)

ihist
```


# Show difference between SSP1 and SSP5
```{r}
diff_rast <- ssp5 - ssp1            # SSP5 minus SSP1, month by month

city_diff <- terra::extract(diff_rast, vect(ukcitiesSf)) %>%
  select(-ID) %>%
  bind_cols(city_name = vect(ukcitiesSf)$city_name, .) %>%
  pivot_longer(-city_name, names_to = "month", values_to = "tmax_diff") %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = month.abb))

# descriptive statistics per city
city_diff %>%
  group_by(city_name) %>%
  summarise(mean_diff   = mean(tmax_diff),
            median_diff = median(tmax_diff),
            min_diff    = min(tmax_diff),
            max_diff    = max(tmax_diff),
            sd_diff     = sd(tmax_diff))

# quick visual
ggplot(city_diff, aes(month, tmax_diff, group = city_name, colour = city_name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(y = "Tmax difference (°C), SSP5 − SSP1, 2081–2100")
```
